result:
I played all 24 months. All three training runs finished on time, all inference demand was served, and there were no penalties. **Final net cost: $1,214.5M.**

| Window | Needed (kH-months) | Delivered |
|---|---|---|
| Months 0–7 | 60 | 152.5 |
| Months 8–15 | 140 | 257.7 |
| Months 16–23 | 320 | 327.4 (last month's figure is my projection) |

**Settlement:** spend $1,359.2M (GPUs $1,040M, cloud contracts $462.7M, power $198.3M, spot $9.8M, minus $351.7M from resales), minus $275.5M for GPUs still held, plus $130.8M of contract and power obligations running past month 23.

**What I did:**
- **Months 0–3 (supply tight):** I ordered 16k gen H GPUs, reserved 12 kH of cloud capacity on 24-month terms before prices went up, and signed power ahead of the deliveries. Used-GPU prices had a 1.1× premium, which gave away whether supply was tight or loose.
- **Gen N timing:** the two launch rumours ("around month 12" and "around month 15") only overlapped at months 13–14. When month 13 passed without a launch, month 14 was nearly certain, so I added 12 MW of power in time for the new GPUs.
- **Month 14 (launch):** I ordered 16k gen N GPUs. All of them shipped between months 16 and 20.
- **Final window:** I added a 4 kH, 6-month reservation and one month of spot to cover month 16 before gen N arrived. From month 17 I sold 12k gen H and 9k gen N GPUs, about $350M in total, while still keeping a buffer of roughly 7 kH-months.

**Where it cost more than it needed to:**
- **Too much capacity early:** the first two windows got about 2.3× more compute than they needed. Much of the early gen H buying and the 24-month reservations were really insurance for the final window, and that surplus has no value outside its own window.
- **Commitments past month 23:** the 24-month reservations and power contracts still owed $131M at settlement.

The month 2 call hung past the 2-minute tool limit, though it completed correctly in the background. I waited rather than re-running it, so the reservation wasn't made twice.
